title: Stalk vanishing for one scalar cone
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let D(\mathcal O_X) be its derived category [def-pc-derived-category], and let g be a compatible family of local sections of \mathcal O_X [def-sc-derived-global-scalar]. Let E\xrightarrow{g}E\to K\to E[1] be a distinguished triangle. If x\in X belongs to D(g(X)), or if H^n(E)_x=0 for every integer n, then H^n(K)_x=0 for every integer n. Here vanishing means that the underlying additive stalk is a subsingleton.

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: The additive stalk functor on module sheaves is exact: forget to abelian sheaves and use exactness of filtered colimits of abelian groups. Apply it degreewise to complexes. It preserves quasi-isomorphisms and commutes with homology, giving the stalks of H^n(E) and H^n(K).

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: The global scalar acts on this stalk complex by multiplication by the germ of its top section, since the family is compatible under restrictions. If x lies in the corresponding basic open, the germ is a unit in the local ring. Its inverse acts as an inverse chain map. The long exact homology sequence of the stalk triangle then makes all H^n(K)_x zero; equivalently the cone of an isomorphism is zero (Tag 05QR).

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: If instead all H^n(E)_x are zero, the terms on both sides of H^n(K)_x in the same long exact sequence vanish. Exactness makes H^n(K)_x zero as well. A zero additive group has a subsingleton carrier.
